content.explanation: Algebraic structures abstract common patterns: groups model symmetry, rings model number systems, fields enable division, vector spaces model linear combinations.
analogies: Like discovering the same blueprint underlies many different buildings
visuals: Venn diagram of algebraic structure hierarchy

practiceProblems.problemText: Decide whether ℤ under subtraction forms a group: check every axiom (closure, associativity, identity, inverses) explicitly and report the first one that fails.
Explain why a field can be described as "two groups sharing one set" and which field property vector spaces require that rings alone do not supply.

misconceptions.statement: A group is just a set with a rule attached
misconceptions.whyItFeelsRight: The definition reads like a formality
misconceptions.structuralReason: The axioms are load-bearing: associativity failures break composition of transformations, and the identity/inverse pair is what makes equations solvable. Drop one axiom and the entire edifice (Lagrange's theorem, symmetry counting) collapses.

comprehended.evidence: Can explain why each axiom matters with examples
